sect1.title: Do I Need Multilib?
sect1.para: Now that multilib has a definition, it is time to decide whether to enable that support. Depending on what you want out of this book, it may be required.

sect2.title: Steam
sect2.para: Steam has a hard requirement on multilib capabilities and demands 32-bit libraries on x86 systems, whilst at the same time not supporting pure 32-bit systems. In order to run Steam on Linux, you need to have an x86_64/AMD64 CPU and many 32-bit libraries, including Xorg, audio, and GPU drivers.

Originally, Steam was a set of 32-bit binaries and began introducing 64-bit only components, like for the store front and eventually the log-in screen. Many have asked for years that Steam should become fully 64-bit. The goal was to no longer require 32-bit libraries at all, no multilib needed. Steam eventually only fulfilled one part of that, which was making Steam 64-bit; at the same time, Steam still requires 32-bit libraries. This will be the case for the foreseeable future. Multilib is absolutely required for Steam.

sect2.title: Wine
sect2.para: Wine can depend on certain things, differing upon the architecture being built. As these architectures require a more in-depth explanation and a roadmap on how to approach things, see which will help you better understand whether you need 32-bit libraries. If you need a given architecture and it says it needs 32-bit libraries, lib32, or MLFS, proceed to the next page. If you don't need those libraries but need the i686 MinGW-w64 toolchain, you won't need multilib for Wine. As a teaser though, if you want the new WoW64 or pure 64-bit mode, multilib is not required for Wine.
